record.paper_title: Open Problems and Conjectures Related to the Theory of Mathematical Quasicrystals
record.original_question: For an aperiodic repetitive tiling of dimension d, does polynomial patch complexity growth p(n)=O(n^d) force the rational Čech cohomology of the tiling space to be finitely generated, i.e. rk(H*(Ω,Q))<∞?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.5.1 With the same notation, is it the case that for an aperiodic, repetitive tiling of dimension d, if p(n) = O(nd), then rk(H∗(Ω, Q)) < ∞?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let T be a tiling of R^d with finite local complexity (only finitely many tile types up to translation, and only finitely many two-tile patches up to translation). Assume T is aperiodic (no nonzero translation maps T to itself) and repetitive (for every patch P appearing in T, there exists R>0 such that every ball of radius R in R^d contains a translate of P). Let the patch-counting (complexity) function p: N → N be defined by

  p(n) = number of distinct patches of T of diameter at most n, counted up to translation.

Let Ω denote the continuous hull (tiling space) of T, namely the completion of the orbit {T - x : x ∈ R^d} in the local topology. Let H*(Ω, Q) denote the Čech cohomology of Ω with rational coefficients.

Question: Does the polynomial complexity bound p(n) = O(n^d) imply that the total rational Čech cohomology has finite rank, i.e. rk(H*(Ω, Q)) < ∞?
artifact.status_search_result: A one-dimensional counterexample by Julien ("Complexity and cohomology for cut-and-projection tilings", Ergodic Theory Dynam. Systems) shows that polynomial patch-counting complexity does not in general force the rational Čech cohomology of the tiling space to be finitely generated; the implication does hold within the restricted class of cut-and-project tilings, but fails for general aperiodic repetitive tilings, answering the question in the negative.

status_evidence.title: Complexity and cohomology for cut and projection tilings
status_evidence.snippet: A link is made between the exponent of the complexity, and the fact that the cohomology of the associated tiling space is finitely generated over Q. We show that such a link cannot be established for more general tilings, and we present a counter-example in dimension one.
status_evidence.claim: There exists a one-dimensional aperiodic repetitive tiling with polynomial complexity whose tiling space has cohomology that is not finitely generated over Q, refuting the implication in general.
